App flow — journeys, screens and navigation

The map of SATOM — how you get from sign-in to the right screen, which menu holds which screens, the eight everyday journeys step by step, how your role changes what you see, and where long operations report back.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
📍 WhereEvery page — sign-in (URL /auth/login) → Global home (URL /) → the sidebar of the ADOM you are in

This page is the map. It shows how you move through SATOM: where you land after signing in, which menu holds which screens, and the path through each everyday task. Each journey links to the article with the full detail. For a tour of the screen itself (top bar, sidebar, footer), see Navigation.

From sign-in to your first screen#

  1. 1Open the consolehttps://satom.example.com — not signed in, you are sent to the sign-in page (/auth/login)
  2. 2Sign InUsername and Password on one form, for local and directory (Active Directory, LDAP, RADIUS) accounts
  3. 3Two-Factor Authenticationonly if you set it up: Authentication code (or a backup code), then Verify
  4. 4Landing pagethe page you were sent from, or the Global home
  5. 5Choose where to workSwitch Product, ‹ Global, or the ADOMs list in the Global sidebar

What decides the landing page. SATOM checks the page that sent you to sign in, which it remembers in the sign-in URL:

  • If you were sent to sign in from a page of the console (an expired session or a bookmark, for example), you go back to that page once you are signed in. SATOM only goes back to an address on its own site, and never to Sign Out.
  • Otherwise you land on /, the Global home. Opening / always puts the browser tab in the Global ADOM.
  • If you open /auth/login while you are already signed in, SATOM sends you to /.
  • If the page belongs to a published app with its own sign-in page, you see that app's sign-in page instead of the console form (see App sign-in).

Entering an ADOM. Switch Product (Select the product you want to manage → Open →), ‹ Global and the Global sidebar's ADOMs list take you to the ADOM's home page:

ADOM Lands on URL
Global Global home /
FortiWeb The Server Policy list of the selected device; the Service Diagram when no device is selected /web/
FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator, FortiGate The ADOM's dashboard /adc/, /faz/, /fac/, /fgt/

If your profile does not include an ADOM, SATOM shows "Your profile does not include the ADOM." and opens Global instead. Sign-in details, two-factor authentication and the session lock are covered in First login. How ADOMs keep data apart is in ADOMs and products.

Screen map#

The sidebar changes with the ADOM. In the Global ADOM the first block is Global; in a device ADOM (FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator, FortiGate) it is Operations, followed by the device's own menu. The groups below are the same in every ADOM. An entry appears only when your profile can open the page behind it.

Menu Main screens URL pattern Permission
Top bar Switch Product, Search, notifications bell, Profile, Sign Out /product/select, /search/, /notifications, /auth/profile, /auth/logout Signed in; Search needs any view permission
Global (Global ADOM) Dashboard (Global home), Architecture, Service Diagram, Monitoring, Incidents, Search, Automation, Plugins, Jobs /, /architecture/, /monitoring/, /incidents/, /jobs/manager Dashboard and Jobs: signed in; the others: a view permission such as monitoring.view; Incidents: operations.view
ADOMs (Global ADOM) One link per product ADOM /product/enter/<adom> ADOMs included in your profile
Operations (device ADOMs) The Global block's pages, plus Device Backups, Import Backup /web/backups/<id>, /web/import-backup/ backups.view; Import Backup: backups.restore
Device menu (for example FortiWeb) All pages, the device's own menu, Server Policy /web/workspace/<id> protection.view to read; write access to change
Monitoring (in Global or Operations) Device health, Metrics, Analysis, Deep monitors, Service Monitor, Analytics, Reports; SATOM health in Global only /monitoring/ and its siblings Any view permission
Automation (in Global or Operations) Scheduler, Upgrade Flow, Migration Report, Change Requests, Certificate Manager, Mass Deploy /web/automations/, /web/upgrade-flow/, /web/change-requests/ Write access (for example operations.apply); Upgrade Flow: backups.create or backups.restore; Change Requests: users.manage
Plugins (in Global or Operations) Published Plugin Studio apps, Report Studio, Lua Studio /apps/<app> Each app: the ADOMs and users ticked in its Settings
Plugin Studio Apps, Data stores, Connections, API Catalog, console /studio/ studio.script_library or studio.python_console
Administrator Access (API Tokens, Audit Log, Groups, Users) · API · Devices (Appliances, Firmware, Device Provisioning…) · Objects · System /appliances/, /users/, /audit/, /web/firmware/ users.manage for the group; each entry also has its own permission (Audit Log: audit.view)
Foot of the sidebar Settings (administrators); a read-only Users list for users.view holders /settings/, /users/ users.manage / users.view

The complete, ADOM-by-ADOM entry list (and which entries are greyed out for which product) is in Navigation. To find a page by what it does instead, use the Concept Map in the footer.

ℹ️Note

In the FortiWeb ADOM, a per-device page (for example Device Backups or the Server Policy list) opened with no device selected sends you to the Service Diagram so you can pick one first.

Core journeys#

Every journey below uses fweb-01 as the appliance. Labels are the ones on screen.

Register a device#

  1. 1Open AppliancesAdministrator → Appliances; without the administrator capability, Appliances is in Operations (Global block in Global)
  2. 2Add ApplianceName, Kind, Host / IP, Port, Username, Password, optional Zone, Line, Department
  3. 3Add Appliance (submit)"Appliance fweb-01 created." and the appliance page opens
  4. 4Test ConnectionConnection OK, or Connection failed: <reason>; correct it with Edit
  5. 5DiscoveryStart discovery; SATOM reads the configuration into its own copy, nothing is written
  6. 6Select ittop bar device area → Switch device → fweb-01

Needs appliances.view to open, write access such as appliances.edit to create, and appliances.apply to discover. Detail: Appliances, Rediscovery, Quick start.

Take and restore a backup#

  1. 1Device BackupsFortiWeb ADOM → Operations → Device Backups (or View Backups on the appliance page)
  2. 2Create Backuptransport Auto (REST → SSH) by default; Create First Backup on an empty vault
  3. 3Track itthe flash points to the Jobs dock; the bell reports Backup ready: fweb-01
  4. 4Restoreappliance page → Restore (administrators)
  5. 5Dry runchoose the stored backup, keep Dry run ticked, Validate / Restore — nothing is sent
  6. 6Live restoreuntick Dry run, type fweb-01 to authorise, Validate / Restore
  7. 7Verifya job takes a pre-restore backup, uploads, waits for the reboot and reads the configuration back

Detail: Device backups, Configuration restore.

Change a FortiWeb server policy#

Every change to a device follows the same guarded path: you see the change before it is sent, SATOM checks it, writes it, reads it back and records it.

  1. 1Select the devicetop bar → Switch device → fweb-01
  2. 2Open the listFortiWeb → Server Policy (FortiWeb → Policy → Server Policy when the build's GUI layout is imported)
  3. 3Editdouble-click a row, press Enter, or Edit
  4. 4Change and Savechanged fields are highlighted until you save
  5. 5Review the changeevery field shown as Was and New before anything is sent
  6. 6Apply to fweb-01template lock, edit lease, reference check and build compatibility are checked first
  7. 7Read-backSATOM re-reads what it wrote and checks the device kept it
  8. 8Auditbefore and after recorded in the audit log; Enable, Disable, Delete, Clone run as a job

SATOM's own policy view (used when no GUI layout is imported) names the review step Confirm change to the live device and the button Apply to device. Detail: Server policies.

Upgrade firmware#

For a maintenance window across several FortiWeb appliances:

  1. 1Upgrade FlowFortiWeb ADOM → Operations → Automation → Upgrade Flow
  2. 2Upgrade tochoose the destination version
  3. 3Run pre-upgrade on selectedstage 1: config backup, health battery (SSH), service validation per appliance
  4. 4Create draftstage 2: one change request that cites the evidence of every appliance
  5. 5Approvestage 3: an administrator approves the change
  6. 6Save as scheduled taskstage 4: rounds of N appliances inside the window
  7. 7Follow executionthe execution page, appliance by appliance (/web/upgrade-flow/change/<id>)

For one appliance, use the appliance page: Upgrade Prep → Run preparation → Raise change request, then, once the change is approved, Upgrade → Validate / Accept with Dry run ticked, then live. A live upgrade outside an approved change is refused. Detail: Upgrade Flow, Firmware upgrade.

Raise and approve a change request#

  1. 1New Change RequestAutomation → Change Requests → New Change Request
  2. 2Type of changeChange type and Risk
  3. 3Scope & windowAffected devices, Window start, Window end
  4. 4Proposed wordingTitle, Reason, Rollback plan, Approval (Manual or External)
  5. 5Create draftthe change is saved as a draft
  6. 6Approvemoves it to approved and records who and when
  7. 7Schedulebinds a one-shot scheduled action at the window start
  8. 8Closethe run closes the change with its outcome; a documentary change uses Mark completed or Mark failed

Detail: Change requests.

Respond to a monitoring alert#

  1. 1Bellthe red counter shows unread notifications; alert notifications go to administrators
  2. 2Open the entryit opens the related page, or the notification on the Notifications page
  3. 3How to resolveWhat it means, Common causes, What to do, Related pages
  4. 4Device healthMonitoring → Device health: each card names the failing signal; Open device
  5. 5Open incidentIncidents (right below Monitoring) → New incident, to track the problem
  6. 6UpdateAdd a note, Add a vendor / L3 ticket, set the status to Resolved when fixed

Detail: Notifications, Device health, Incidents, Alerting.

Build and publish a Plugin Studio app#

  1. 1New appPlugin Studio → New app → Flow
  2. 2SettingsWhere it appears (ADOMs) and Who may use it, then Save settings
  3. 3FormAdd field for each input, then Save form
  4. 4DiagramAdd a step, join the steps, Save diagram, then Analyze
  5. 5Testtick Rehearsal, then Run the saved draft — nothing is written
  6. 6Publishclear Fix before publishing, then Publish
  7. 7Use itthe app appears under Plugins for the chosen ADOMs and users (/apps/<app>)

Detail: Your first Plugin Studio app.

Create a profile and a user (administrators)#

  1. 1ProfilesSettings → Access & Identity → Profiles → New Profile
  2. 2Name itProfile name, then Create & set permissions
  3. 3Permissionstick the permissions, then Save permissions
  4. 4UsersAdministrator → Users → Add User
  5. 5Fill inUsername, Password (at least 12 characters), Confirm Password, Profile
  6. 6Create User"User <name> created." — the user's next request uses the profile

Detail: Users and profiles.

How your role changes the flow#

The three system profiles are Viewer (readonly), Operator and Administrator. A custom profile can mix any permissions; the table shows the system profiles.

Journey Viewer Operator Admin
Sidebar Global or Operations, Monitoring, device menu, Jobs Adds Automation (Scheduler, Upgrade Flow, Migration Report, provisioning) and Scout (when configured) Adds Administrator, Change Requests, Certificate Manager, Calendar, Plugin Studio, Settings
Audit log Readable at /audit/; no sidebar link Readable at /audit/; no sidebar link Administrator → Audit Log
Register a device No Yes Yes
Backups List the vault Create, upload, download Also restore
Change a policy Read only Yes Yes
Upgrade firmware No Prep and dry run; a live upgrade needs an approved change Raises, approves and schedules the change
Change requests No No Yes
Plugin Studio No No Yes; published apps go to whoever they are given to
Users and profiles No No Yes
Jobs Own jobs Own jobs Every user's jobs

What you see without a permission#

  • The menu entry is not drawn. The sidebar asks the same permission as the page, so a link never leads to a refusal.
  • Buttons are hidden. For example a viewer sees no Create Backup in the vault, and the server policy view says "Read-only: changing this policy needs the config_write permission."
  • A direct URL answers 403. The page Access denied — You don't have permission to view this page. offers Return home.
  • An ADOM outside your profile sends you to Global with "Your profile does not include the ADOM."
  • Another user's job, or a change request outside your ADOM, answers 404 rather than revealing that it exists.
  • Signed out, any page sends you to sign in with "Please log in to access this page."

A greyed-out entry with a slash icon is not about your permissions: the page does not work for that ADOM's product. Hover it to read why. See Navigation and Permissions.

Where long operations go#

Anything that talks to an appliance and takes longer than a moment becomes a job. You never have to wait on the page.

You started It runs as You get back to it from
A device action from a button (backup, bulk policy action, hardware scan) A job with a toast in the Jobs dock that follows you across pages View job → in the dock, or Jobs in the sidebar (/jobs/manager)
A device action from a form (restore, upgrade) The wait page (/jobs/<id>/wait) Keep working — it continues in the background, Open in Jobs, Show result
A finished or failed job, an alert A notification The bell, View all notifications › (/notifications), Open related page
Any write An audit entry Administrator → Audit Log, or /audit/ for any audit.view holder; searchable by user, action and entry ID
A scheduled change A scheduled action bound to the change request Automation → Scheduler, the change request's page, the Calendar
A firmware flash A before/after report Firmware Reports on the appliance page

Leaving a wait page stops nothing. Detail: Jobs, Notifications, Audit log.
